BMI for men: interpreting the number in context

Adult BMI cutoffs are the same for men and women, but body composition and fat distribution can shape the conversation.

Written by Elena Morris, CHCW · Medically reviewed by Dr. Daniel Chen, MD · Updated July 24, 2026

Answer: Standard adult BMI categories for men are below 18.5, 18.5–24.9, 25–29.9, and 30+. A BMI result does not distinguish fat from muscle.

Muscle and BMI

Men who train for strength or carry considerable muscle may have a BMI in an “overweight” range without having a high body-fat level. Fitness, waist circumference, blood pressure, and laboratory markers often add useful detail.

Abdominal weight matters

Men are more likely to store fat around the abdomen, a pattern associated with cardiometabolic risk. If you are concerned, ask a clinician whether a waist measurement and broader risk review would be useful.

Practical next steps

Focus on a pattern of regular movement, strength work, plants and fibre, adequate protein, and sleep. A number on the scale is only one data point.
